source_findings: Synchronizers are timestamp-driven: ExactTime requires identical message timestamps; ApproximateTime matches on message/header timestamps within a bounded tolerance/policy rather than assuming arrival order.

The Python ApproximateTime implementation exposes queue_size and slop and explicitly warns that headerless current-time fallback and sync_arrival_time should be avoided because delays are unpredictable.

The current C++ ApproximateTime policy uses a typed TimeGetter, bounded per-input queues, an explicit max_interval_duration, inter-message lower-bound checks, an age penalty, dropped-message tracking and deterministic candidate/pivot search.
When a per-topic queue exceeds queue_size, the oldest message on that topic is dropped; any active candidate is invalidated and recomputed.
The C++ source detects out-of-order message timestamps and warns, but does not itself implement F2's stronger explicit UNKNOWN/UNALIGNED clock-domain relation or fail-closed fusion authority.
The source is a useful mechanism comparator, but importing ROS 2/message_filters would add a much larger dependency surface than the small deterministic F2-WP-711 contract requires.

thin_native_rules: Use explicit source event-time from typed observations as the primary fusion coordinate; never silently substitute arrival time.
Bound each source queue/window and preserve exact drop/rejection diagnostics.
Require an explicit maximum admissible cross-source event-time span before constructing a fusion set.
Invalidate/recompute a candidate when evidence it depended on was dropped or became stale.
Keep F2's stronger clock-domain identity, skew/uncertainty and UNKNOWN/UNALIGNED semantics instead of inheriting ROS assumptions.
Do not copy age-penalty/pivot heuristics unless an F2 ablation shows value over a simpler deterministic admissibility rule.

counterhypothesis: A fixed deterministic fusion-window rule over typed F2 observations may already capture all useful behavior; ROS ApproximateTime's candidate optimization and age penalty may add complexity without improving correctness or latency.
next_falsifier: After WP-711 source implementation exists, compare simple explicit-window selection against a pivot/age-penalty variant on synthetic skew, out-of-order, missing-source, stale-source and burst workloads; measure fusion correctness, rejected/unknown cases, queue occupancy and decision latency.
architecture_delta: NO_NEW_DELTA_REQUIRED_AT_E1: current WP-711 scope already contains the strongest source-supported invariants; this E1 chiefly supports the no-arrival-order and bounded-window design and argues against importing ROS2.
